newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI IS YOUNGEST WORLD CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI IS YOUNGEST WORLD CHAMPION.

text.p: Tara Lipinski became the youngest-ever world women's figure skating champion with a performance of astonishing maturity and sustained brilliance on Saturday.
The tiny American, at 14 years nine months and 12 days is 32 days younger than Norwegian Sonie Henie when she won the first of her 10 successive world titles in 1927.
"I never expected this, particularly this year. It's a big shock, but I love it," Lipinski said.
Team mate and defending champion Michelle Kwan took second place with France's Vanessa Gusmeroli third.

Ironically, the 1.47 metres, 35 kgs Lipinski was technically ineligible for this competition under a rule passed last June that stated skaters had to be 15 the previous July 1 to take part. But she was given a dispensation because she competed last year before the rule was brought in. She was 15th a year ago.
On Saturday Lipinski accomplished seven triple jumps including a difficult triple loop-triple loop combination that no other skater in the world can yet perform.
She did not put a foot wrong in her four-minute display although she again relied on her fast body spins to complete her jumps because she gets little height on take off.
"I wasn't worried about what the others did," said Lipinski, who skated second in the final group of six. "I went out and skated the best I could, then it was up to the judges."
They awarded her four scores of 5.9 and five of 5.8 for technique with less impressive numbers for artistry.
Despite Lipinski's outstanding display, Kwan had the better free skate score as she rediscovered her best form to advance from fourth to second.
She gleaned just one 5.9 for technique but had seven for artistry.
It was Kwan's best performance since her short programme last month at the U.S. Nationals. She fell twice in the subsequent long programme and lost the title to Lipinski.
Kwan gave a superb display to Indian music, slipping up only to double out of a planned triple lutz late in her routine.
"I've put a lot of pressure on myself this season and began thinking about the wrong things," said 16-year-old Kwan.
"I had to get back to having fun again and stop behaving like a headless chicken."
Gusmeroli, sixth at the European championships after a poor free programme, showed she had learned from that with a fine display to circus music.
"I have worked hard on my long programme since the Europeans and it showed in the qualifying on Monday and again today," she said. "I have made constant progress."
Gusmeroli was her country's water skiing champion two years ago and still participates in the sport for fun.
European champion Irina Slutskaya of Russia advanced two places to fourth and just missed out on helping Kwan to victory.
Kwan, Lipinski and Slutskaya all had three first place votes from the judges for their free skating.
Kwan won the section because all her other votes were for second place.
Lipinski was second in the section but if two more judges had preferred Slutskaya to Lipinski the Russian would have been second for the section and Kwan would have retained her title.
Lipinski finished with 2.5 factored placements -- 0.5 for winning the short and 2.0 for being second in the free.
Kwan had 3.0 for being fourth and first while Gusmeroli finished with 5.0.
